email_messages.subject: Q2 Warehouse Slotting Pilot — Kickoff & Data Needed by Friday
email_messages.body:
Hi David, Sarah,

As discussed in last week’s ops sync, we’re kicking off the Q2 slotting optimization pilot for the Dallas and Joliet sites. Goal is to reduce pick travel time and improve dock-to-stock throughput for our top 20 SKUs by volume.

To build the baseline, can you please send the following by EOD Friday?

1) Last 8 weeks of order lines (CSV export is fine)
2) Current bin locations and replenishment triggers
3) Any known constraints (hazmat segregation, temp zones, customer-specific handling)

Proposed kickoff: Tuesday 10:00–10:45 CT. Jason is CC’d in case we need WMS report support.

Thanks,
Maria

Maria Chen
Operations Program Manager | HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: Re: Q2 Warehouse Slotting Pilot — Kickoff & Data Needed by Friday
email_messages.body:
Hi Maria,

Confirmed—Joliet can provide the 8-week order line export and current bin map by Friday noon CT.

A couple notes for constraints:
- We have a dedicated overpack area for two customers (Riverton and Kestrel) that can’t be mixed due to QA requirements.
- Hazmat is currently in Zone H with fixed aisle allocation; we can adjust within the zone but not relocate outside.

Tuesday 10:00–10:45 CT works for me.

Thanks,
David

David Nguyen
Senior Warehouse Manager | HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: Customer Feedback: On-time Performance Survey Results (March) — Action Items
email_messages.body:
Hi Maria, Megan,

Sharing a quick readout from the March customer satisfaction pulse focused on on-time performance and shipment visibility.

Highlights:
- Overall satisfaction: 4.2/5 (up from 4.0 in Feb)
- Top praise: faster exception notifications; cleaner POD uploads
- Top gaps:
  1) “Late appointment updates” when dwell > 2 hours at select cross-docks
  2) “Inconsistent tracking milestones” on LTL moves routed through the Midwest

Proposed action items:
- Ops: standardize the dwell escalation at 90 minutes (vs. current site-by-site thresholds)
- IT/Ops: audit milestone mapping for the two carriers flagged most often (I can send names in a separate note)
- Customer Success: refresh the shipment visibility FAQ and circulate to CS reps

Can we align on owners in next week’s cross-functional standup?

Thanks,
Sarah

Sarah Patel
Customer Experience Lead | HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: Re: Quick check — any Finance Ops changes impacting reimbursements?
email_messages.body:
Hi David,

As we’re finalizing the internal controls notes for Q2, can you confirm whether Finance Ops rolled out any updates that impacted employee reimbursements? I’ve heard a couple of managers mention “new receipt requirements” and an “expense coding field,” but I don’t have the specifics.

If there was a change, I also need to note whether it touches contract workflows (e.g., redline approval) or if it’s strictly T&E.

Thanks,
Maria

Maria Chen
Finance Operations Program Manager
HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: Re: Quick check — any Finance Ops changes impacting reimbursements?
email_messages.body:
Hi Maria,

Yes—Finance Ops updated the travel and expense (T&E) policy effective 4/1.

Key items impacting reimbursements:
- Rideshare: itemized receipts are now required for rideshare charges over $25 (previously we accepted non-itemized email confirmations regardless of amount).
- Concur/expense submission: we introduced a new required expense coding field (cost object/GL coding) so reimbursements post to the correct lane/region programs without manual reclass.

This is strictly an internal reimbursement control change. It does not affect the contract redline approval process or any customer contract workflow—those approvals still route through Legal/RevOps as before.

If you need the exact policy language, Megan has the FAQ that went out with the rollout.

Best,
David

David Nguyen
Director, Finance Operations
HelioFreight Logistics

email_messages.subject: Re: Quick check — any Finance Ops changes impacting reimbursements?
email_messages.body:
Adding the employee-facing context in case it’s helpful for your controls notes.

We made the change because we were seeing inconsistent backup for higher-dollar rideshare claims and too many manual corrections during month-end close. The new expense coding field is required at submission (Concur won’t allow “unknown” anymore), which should reduce reclasses and speed reimbursement once reports are approved.

Agree with David: this is limited to T&E reimbursements and doesn’t touch contract redlines/approvals.

Thanks,
Megan

Megan Ortiz
Manager, Travel & Expense (Finance Ops)
HelioFreight Logistics
